title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative: ILO engagement with employers in the Philippines has increasingly focused on helping enterprises respond to rising trade, ESG and labour-standard expectations. The 2026–2027 programme deepens this employer-facing offer and links it more explicitly to trade exposure and policy reform. Employers are actively engaged—together with the ILO—in national discussions on wage-setting, social protection reform, OSH, labour migration and the current development of a National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights, building on the CHRP’s National Baseline Assessment. This engagement is reinforced through ongoing ILO projects that provide practical entry points to translate policy commitments—such as the Trabaho Para sa Bayan Plan, OSH strategy, and emerging ESG frameworks—into employer guidance and enterprise-level action, while strengthening the evidence base for policy advocacy. A key priority for the next biennium will be scaling sectoral engagement, including the expansion of ESG and HRDD tools to priority export sectors and the introduction of a new stream of work in the mining sector, which is highly exposed to international scrutiny around labour standards, environmental performance, community impacts and supply-chain due diligence. Mining will be strategically important given its links to critical minerals, energy transition supply chains and trade relations, and will require early employer engagement to ensure that emerging ESG, OSH and HRDD expectations are practical, proportionate and aligned with international labour standards. The ILO–EBMO partnership will also continue to support skills development, just transition dialogue, implementation of Convention No. 190 on violence and harassment, and OSH reform in line with Convention No. 155, ensuring that employer perspectives are embedded in national frameworks while enterprises receive practical support to comply.
